issues.issue: The dates and words are garbled ("FES. 12, 2006", "THES POLICY"), but nothing in the garbling changes the operative meaning of the policy period or the insuring promise.

"BLANKET BUILDING ... LIMIT: $7,207,200" with "(BLANKET SUMMARY INFORMATION)" does not say whether that figure is one blanket limit spanning all nine described premises or a summary of separate per-building limits. The same entry also stacks "REPLACEMENT COST", "COINSURANCE: 100%" and "INFLATION GUARD: 4%" without saying which value they are measured against.

The blanket limit must be squared with the Coinsurance Additional Condition (F.1.a/F.1.b), which computes the penalty from "the Limit of Insurance for the property" and from "value of Covered Property at the time of loss" — terms that have no single meaning when one limit covers nine buildings.
The blanket contents entry gives a single $45,000 limit at 100% coinsurance without identifying whose or which contents at which of nine premises it covers.

The caption "BLANKET BUSINESS INCOME RENTAL ... PROP INCL EXTRA EXPENSE" does not identify which of the three coverage options is bought, so whether the $1,099,200 limit covers Business Income including "Rental Value" or "Rental Value" only is genuinely unclear.
Section A.1 of the Business Income form (c189) makes everything depend on which of options a., b. or c. "is selected" in the Declarations, and this Declarations entry does not select one.

"[S]ome conditions may be changed by the attachment of a state amendatory endorsement" identifies no conditions and no ordering rule, leaving the priority between the printed Common Conditions and the Kansas Changes endorsements to be worked out.
"[A]dvance written notice of cancellation" fixes no minimum notice period, so how much advance notice suffices cannot be read off the clause.

This paragraph is expressly replaced by Paragraph A.2.a of the Kansas Cancellation endorsement (c247), which restates the same notice periods but adds a duty to state reasons, so two differently worded versions of the same condition sit in the policy.
"[T]he refund may be less than pro rata" states no method or floor for computing the short-rate refund.

The clause says the first Named Insured "is authorized to make changes in the terms of this policy with our consent" and then that terms "can be amended or waived only by endorsement", two mechanisms for change that are not reconciled within the same paragraph.

The sentence disclaiming inspections is broken mid-clause ("any such « IN Ioan NaWioadS and the premiums to be charged"), so the scope of what the insurer disclaims cannot be read from the text as printed.

It applies "Paragraphs 1. and 2. of this condition", but the Inspections and Surveys condition as printed in this policy (c015, c016) carries no such numbering, leaving the cross-reference to be reconstructed.
The carve-out is keyed to "Paragraph 2. of this condition", which is not numbered anywhere in the printed Inspections and Surveys condition (c015-c016).

"[W]e will assume you no longer want the insurance" and the discretion to "reinstate", issue a new policy, or return a late payment leaves the insured with no way to tell which outcome follows a late installment.

The Kansas Changes endorsement (c260) replaces this condition with one that merely bars payment for the affected loss rather than voiding the whole Coverage Part, so two inconsistent fraud consequences appear in the same instrument.

The Kansas Changes endorsement (c254) states that the Control Of Property Condition "is superseded and replaced" with a differently worded provision, leaving two versions of the condition in the policy.

This location-by-location breach rule is restated in different words by the Kansas Changes Control of Property provision (c254), which says coverage is lost "at the involved location" — a formulation that does not plainly match this one.
This condition sets a 2-year suit limitation while the Kansas Changes endorsement (c251) replaces it with a 5-year limitation, a direct contradiction on the face of the policy.

As printed the sentence reads that a person other than you having custody of Covered Property "will benefit from this insurance", the opposite of the No Benefit To Bailee heading, because the negation has dropped out.
The waiver right is keyed to loss to "your Covered Property or Covered Income", but "Covered Income" appears nowhere else in the policy as a defined term.
The definition is truncated to "include radioacti\ explosive propertles", so the list of hazardous properties cannot be read from the text.
"'Nuclear material' means 'source material - nuclear material' or 'by-product material'" drops the word "special" and the punctuation, so one of the three defined categories is unreadable.
The definition is broken mid-sentence ("'Source material,' 'special nuclear material,' Atomic Energy Act of 1954 or in any law ame, thereof"), omitting the operative verb entirely.

The clause makes the insured a voting "member" of a mutual insurer, which sits awkwardly with the Declarations naming State Auto Property and Casualty Insurance Company and with the Non-Assessable condition (c046).

Non-assessability of "any premium other than that stated in this policy" is hard to square with the Premium Audit condition (c302), under which audited earned premium may exceed the advance premium stated in the Declarations.

This form defines "you" as the Named Insured shown in the Declarations, while the CGL definition (c261) extends "you" to any other person or organization qualifying as a Named Insured, so the same pronoun has two scopes in one policy.
"[D]irect physical loss of or damage to Covered Property" is the classic trigger phrase whose boundary (physical alteration versus loss of use or function) the clause does not define.

Sub-paragraph (5) covers additions under construction and materials "if not covered by other Insurance", a condition whose operation is left to be worked out, and the paragraph is interrupted by unreadable characters.

Item k. excludes property "covered under another coverage form of this or any other policy in which it is more specifically described", and "more specifically described" gives no workable test for which form governs.

The two caps interact awkwardly: (a) makes the Limit of Insurance the ceiling for loss plus debris removal, while (b) sets debris removal at 25% of "the sum of the deductible plus the amount that we pay", so the base of the percentage is not self-evident.

"[T]he increased costs incurred to comply with enforcement of an ordinance or law in the course of repair, rebuilding or replacement of damaged parts of that property" leaves open whether costs of rebuilding undamaged parts required by code are within it.

The coverage runs against Exclusion B.1.a, Ordinance Or Law (c149), which excludes increased costs of complying with an ordinance following a physical loss; the two are reconciled only by the partial carve-out in e.(8) (c070).
The paragraph is misnumbered "(7)" although e.(2) refers to it as e.(3), so the cross-reference chain in this Additional Coverage does not line up.
The paragraph opens with an orphan word "loss." carried over from the preceding text, and its (a)/(b) conditions are joined by "and", so whether both must be shown is left to construction.
This entry reproduces the whole of the prior-noncompliance paragraph (c066) verbatim before adding the pollutants/fungus exclusion, so the same words appear twice as separate operative paragraphs.

For a building insured under a blanket limit the cap turns on "the value of the damaged building as of the time of loss", and the form never says whether that value is actual cash value or replacement cost.
The blanket-limit formula has to be applied to the single $7,207,200 Blanket Building limit in the Declarations (c002), which does not allocate any per-building limit or value.

Payment is withheld "[u]ntil the property is actually repaired or replaced" and unless repairs are made "as soon as reasonably possible after the loss or damage, not to exceed two years", and "as soon as reasonably possible" supplies no measurable benchmark.

The clause disapplies the Ordinance or Law Exclusion only "to the extent that such Exclusion would conflict" with this Additional Coverage, a formula that itself requires a court to decide how far the conflict runs.
It is a partial override of Exclusion B.1.a, Ordinance Or Law (c149), and the two provisions cannot be applied together without deciding where one stops and the other begins.

It coordinates with the Loss Payment (c112), Valuation (c122) and Replacement Cost (c142) provisions, all of which likewise exclude ordinance-driven increased cost, so the boundary between those exclusions and this Additional Coverage must be drawn.
The trigger "[i]f a Coinsurance percentage of 80% or more or, a Value Reporting period symbol, is shown" is broken by a stray comma, obscuring whether both or either condition opens the Extensions.
It conditions coverage on the Causes Of Loss — Broad Form applying, but the Declarations show only the Special Form, so the paragraph has no field of operation in this policy.
The $250 per tree, shrub or plant sub-limit stated here is raised to $500 by the Kansas Changes endorsement (c257), so two different figures appear in the policy.

"[T]he applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations" for "any one occurrence" does not say how the single blanket limit is applied when one occurrence damages property at more than one described premises.
It has to be read with the Blanket Building entry in the Declarations (c002), which shows one limit across nine separately described premises.

The rule that losses to separate items "will not be combined" when "separate Limits of Insurance apply", coupled with "the Deductible will be applied only once per occurrence", does not resolve how the $5,000 deductible falls when nine buildings share one blanket limit.
The sequence here (reduce for coinsurance, then subtract the deductible) must be matched against the Coinsurance Condition's own Steps (3) and (4) (c126), which also subtract the deductible.
The list of what each party bears is mangled (").@Bear the other expenses of the appraisal Rand umplre equally"), and the "pay its chosen appraiser" limb has dropped out entirely.

This condition makes appraisal available on one party's written demand, while the Kansas Changes endorsement (c259) replaces it with a provision under which "an appraisal will be made only if both you and we agree, voluntarily" — a direct contradiction.
"[P]rompt notice" fixes no period and is measured against nothing in the clause.
"Take all reasonable steps to protect the Covered Property from further damage" sets a standard whose content the clause does not specify.

"[A]t our option, we will either" pay value, pay repair cost, take the property, or repair/rebuild/replace "with other property of like kind and quality", without any standard governing how that election is made.
The insurer's free election here has to be squared with the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (c137, c140), which fixes the measure of recovery and its conditions.

It excludes ordinance-driven increased cost from the cost to repair, rebuild or replace, which must be reconciled with the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (c064, c071) that supplies exactly that cost.
"[Y]our financial interest in the Covered Property" is undefined and could mean equity, cost basis, or insurable interest.

Vacancy turns on whether "at least 31% of its total square footage" is rented and "[u]sed by the lessee ... to conduct its customary operations", a test whose application to residential apartment tenants is not obvious.

The 15% reduction for a building "vacant for more than 60 consecutive days" applies building-by-building, but neither this clause nor the vacancy definition says how it operates where one blanket limit covers nine buildings.

This makes actual cash value the default measure, while the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (c137) states that replacement cost "replaces Actual Cash Value in the Loss Condition, Valuation"; which governs, and when, is not settled on the face of either.
Valuation switches on whether "you make repairs promptly", a term the form nowhere defines or bounds.

The whole formula runs off "the value of Covered Property at the time of loss", and the form never says whether that value is actual cash value or replacement cost — the choice that decides whether any coinsurance penalty exists at all.

The valuation input has to be taken from the Valuation condition (c121, actual cash value) or the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (c137), which point to different figures, and it must then be applied to the single blanket limit in the Declarations (c002).
"[T]wo or more separate items" is not defined, so whether nine separately described apartment buildings are "items" to be totalled under one blanket limit is left open.
It must be applied to the Blanket Building limit in the Declarations (c002) and read alongside the Deductible condition (c099), which by contrast forbids combining losses where separate limits apply.
This paragraph b. is replaced for townhouse coverage by the Kansas Changes endorsement (c256), which directs payment to an Insurance Trustee, first mortgagees and the Association instead.

The paragraph is a merge of two unrelated provisions — the mortgageholder subrogation text and the Agreed Value/Inflation Guard Optional Coverage text — so no single operative rule can be read out of it.
The Agreed Value Optional Coverage is expressed to apply only if shown in the Declarations, and no Agreed Value or Agreed Value expiration date appears in this policy's Declarations.
The Inflation Guard text is interleaved with mortgageholder and cancellation-notice sentences, so the three-step formula for the automatic increase cannot be read continuously.
The 4% Inflation Guard shown in the Declarations (c002) increases the Limit of Insurance during the term, which bears directly on the Coinsurance computation (c126) but is nowhere reconciled with it.
The paragraph breaks off at "if we cancel for any other If:" and is interleaved with Inflation Guard text, so the second notice period is incomplete.
The sentence is cut off ("at The number of davs ° least 10 days before the expiration date of") and never states what notice is owed.

The Replacement Cost paragraph is spliced together with Agreed Value text, so the operative sentence — that "Replacement Cost (without deduction for depreciation) replaces Actual Cash Value in the Loss Condition, Valuation" — is separated from its own opening words and its reach is not readable as printed.

Saying replacement cost simply "replaces Actual Cash Value" in the Valuation condition (c121) cannot be squared with G.3.d (c140), which forbids paying on a replacement cost basis until the property is actually repaired or replaced.
Replacement Cost is excluded for "[c]ontents of a residence", a phrase that gives no answer for an apartment complex where the insured buildings are residences occupied by tenants.

The insured may claim actual cash value and "still make a claim for the additional coverage this Optional Coverage provides" if notice is given within 180 days, but the clause does not say whether the later replacement-cost claim remains subject to G.3.d's actual-repair condition.

Payment is conditioned on the property being "actually repaired or replaced" and on repairs being made "as soon as reasonably possible after the loss or damage", a period with no outer date and no benchmark.
The condition qualifies the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (c137), which states flatly that replacement cost replaces actual cash value in the Valuation condition, and the two are not reconciled.

The cap is the least of the limit, the cost to replace "[o]f comparable material and quality", and "[t]he amount actually spent" — terms that leave open whether an insured who has not yet spent anything can recover replacement cost at all.
It excludes ordinance-driven increased cost from replacement cost, which has to be squared with the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (c064) and its e.(9) coordination clause (c071).
"Pollutants" is defined by an open catch-all — "any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant" followed by illustrative examples — whose outer reach the definition does not fix.
"Risks Of Direct Physical Loss" is stated without definition, and the reference to loss "Umited in Section C." is misspelled.

The lead-in excludes loss "caused directly or indirectly" by the listed perils "regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence", an anti-concurrent-cause formula whose reach against a covered fire loss is not fixed by the text.

Exclusion B.1.a, Ordinance Or Law, bars the increased costs of complying with an ordinance after a loss, which the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (c064) and its e.(8) override (c070) expressly pay.
The two printed columns have run together, so exclusions d., e., f., g. and h. are interleaved with the alcohol and employer's-liability text and cannot be read as continuous provisions.

The two printed columns have run together, so the 3.a. weather-conditions exclusion is interleaved with the freezing and dishonesty exclusions and paragraph 3.c. breaks off at "described premises" without its ensuing-loss exception.

Sub-paragraph (4)(a) excludes increased loss from delay in rebuilding caused by "interference at the location ... by strikers or other persons", and the catch-all "or other persons" against the single specific "strikers" leaves the exclusion's reach open; "(6) Any other consequential loss" is a second unbounded catch-all.

The exclusion of loss from delay in rebuilding must be read against the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which itself measures the loss period by when property "should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed".
It disapplies an exclusion for the Leasehold Interest Coverage Form, which is not among the forms scheduled in this policy's Declarations.
It operates on the Leasehold Interest Coverage Form, which this policy does not include.
It operates on the Legal Liability Coverage Form, which is not scheduled in this policy's Declarations.
It adds exclusions to the Legal Liability Coverage Form, a form this policy does not contain.
"[A]n abrupt falling down or caving in" with the result that the building "cannot be occupied for its intended purpose" leaves the degree of structural failure required unspecified.

The paragraph runs into unrelated text at the end ("even if use of ocd 2 live material of methods, In construct remodeling or renovation, contributes to tt collapse"), so limb f. is not legible as written.

The entry begins with a duplicate of paragraph 2.f. and the sentence "The criteria set forth in 1.a. through 1.d. do af tt loss listed In 2.a., 2.d. and 2.e." is incomplete, so the rule for outdoor property cannot be read.

The prerequisite that "all reasonable means were used to save and preserve the property from further damage" is an unmeasured standard, and the reference to "E.2. and E.6." does not match the paragraph numbering that follows.

Three different provisions — the fungus Business Income limb, the Property In Transit extension and the Water Damage extension — are interleaved line by line, so neither the 30-day fungus sub-limit nor its conditions can be read continuously.
The entry opens with stray fungus/period-of-restoration text before the Glass extension begins, so the provision's own opening words are absent.

The endorsement deletes "the second and third paragraphs" of Civil Authority and substitutes a single sentence, but it does not say which of the printed paragraphs those are or what becomes of the 72-hour waiting period and the Extra Expense limb.
As printed, the Civil Authority Additional Coverage (c197) does not have the paragraph structure this endorsement assumes, so it cannot be applied to that clause without reconstruction.

The substituted paragraph a. makes the period of restoration begin "[i]mmediately after the time of direct physical loss", collapsing the printed form's separate start dates for Business Income and for Extra Expense into one.
It contradicts paragraph a. of the "Period of Restoration" definition in the Business Income form (c240), which begins Business Income coverage only 72 hours after the loss.
"Continuing normal operating expenses incurred, including payroll" does not say which expenses continue or how they are separated from expenses that cease when the building is destroyed.

The whole clause turns on which option "is selected" in the Declarations, but the Declarations entry (c004) reads "BLANKET BUSINESS INCOME RENTAL ... PROP INCL EXTRA EXPENSE" and selects none of a., b. or c.

The promise is to pay "the actual loss of Business Income you sustain due to the necessary 'suspension' of your 'operations' during the 'period of restoration'", and both "actual loss ... you sustain" and "necessary" suspension are left undefined as measures of recovery.

The length of the recovery is fixed entirely by the "period of restoration" definition (c240) as amended by the CP 15 56 endorsement (c185), and those two provisions do not give a single answer for a destroyed apartment building.

"[N]ecessary expenses you incur during the 'period of restoration' that you would not have incurred" is qualified by "[a]void or minimize" the suspension, without any standard for measuring necessity.
The CP 15 56 endorsement (c184) purports to delete the second and third paragraphs of this coverage and substitute a single sentence, which cannot be mapped onto the paragraphs printed here.

The extended period begins only when property "is actually repaired, rebuilt or replaced and 'operations' are resumed" and ends when the insured "could restore" income "with reasonable speed", a standard the clause does not define.

The Extended "Rental Value" text is interleaved with the Interruption Of Computer Operations paragraphs, so the sentence beginning "lf the necessary 'suspension' of your 'operations' produces a 'Rental Value' loss" is split from its own conclusion.

Its trigger — the date property "is actually repaired, rebuilt or replaced and tenantability is restored" — has to be reconciled with the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which ends when property merely "should be repaired".

The Interruption Of Computer Operations text is interleaved line by line with the Extended "Rental Value" provision, so the grant of coverage and its Causes of Loss conditions cannot be read as one provision.

The carry-forward sentence is corrupted ("If loss payment relaling to the first interruptlon does not enraey this amount, then the balance is ilé able ..."), obscuring how an unexhausted balance moves between policy years.

"[T]he applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations" for "any one occurrence" does not explain how the single blanket Business Income limit is applied when the occurrence affects several described premises.
It has to be applied to the Blanket Business Income entry in the Declarations (c004), which shows one $1,099,200 figure with no per-premises allocation.

The Kansas Changes endorsement (c259) replaces "The Appraisal Loss Condition" with a voluntary-only appraisal, and it is not clear whether that replacement reaches this separate Appraisal condition in the Business Income form, which allows appraisal on one party's demand.
"[Y]ou must resume all or part of your 'operations' as quickly as possible" sets an unmeasured duty whose breach is not defined anywhere in the form.

It overlaps with the Loss Determination rule for failure to resume (c226), which imposes a payment consequence for the same conduct without saying whether the duty here is also a condition of coverage.

The measure rests on "[t]he likely Net Income of the business if no physical loss or damage had occurred" and on operating expenses "necessary to resume 'operations' with the same quality of service", neither of which is defined or given a method of proof.

For a rental-value claim these Net Income inputs have to be matched against the "Rental Value" definition (c242), which measures loss by rental income from tenant occupancy rather than by business Net Income.

The reduction applies "to the extent you can resume your 'operations', in whole or in part, by using damaged or undamaged property ... at the described premises or elsewhere", without saying what makes such resumption possible or reasonable.
Recovery is capped by "the length of time it would have taken to resume 'operations' as quickly as possible", a hypothetical period the clause supplies no method of measuring.

This hypothetical-resumption cap sits alongside the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which fixes the end of coverage by when property "should be repaired ... with reasonable speed"; the two set different clocks for the same loss.

The penalty runs off Net Income and operating expenses "that would have been earned or incurred (had no loss occurred) ... for the 12 months following the inception", a hypothetical figure the clause gives no method of fixing.
It must be applied to the blanket Business Income limit in the Declarations (c004) at 100% coinsurance without any per-premises allocation of the underlying rental income.
The deduction list is interleaved with the worked example ("Step 1: . $400,000 x 50% = $200,000") and its numbering runs 1, 2, 3 then jumps, so several deductible expense categories are unreadable.
The Optional Coverages apply only "[i]f shown as applicable in the Declarations", and the Declarations for this policy (c004) show no Maximum Period Of Indemnity.
This 120-day cap would displace the "period of restoration" measure, but no Maximum Period Of Indemnity option is shown in the Declarations (c004).
No Monthly Limit Of Indemnity is shown in the Declarations (c004), so this Coinsurance carve-out has no field of operation.
The limit depends on "[t]he fraction shown in the Declarations for this Optional Coverage", and no such fraction appears in this policy's Declarations (c004).
Activation requires an Agreed Value shown in the Declarations, and none is shown for Business Income in this policy (c004).

The clause replaces the number "30" in the Extended Business Income provisions with "the number shown in the Declarations for this Optional Coverage", but no such number appears in this policy's Declarations.
"Operations" includes "the tenantability of the described premises", a term the form never defines even though it decides when a rental-value suspension begins and ends.

Limb b. applies only "if coverage for Business Income including 'Rental Value' or 'Rental Value' applies", and the Declarations entry (c004) does not identify which of the A.1 options (c189) was selected.

The period ends on "[t]he date when the property at the described premises should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality" — a hypothetical date fixed by "should" and "reasonable speed", neither of which the policy defines or benchmarks.
Paragraph a. as printed (72 hours for Business Income) is contradicted by the CP 15 56 Business Income Changes endorsement (c185), which makes the period begin immediately after the loss.

"Rental Value" is defined as Net Income "that would have been earned ... as rental income from tenant occupancy of the premises described in the Declarations as furnished and equipped by you", which does not say whether it is measured by pre-loss rents, market rents, or actual re-let experience.
It must be worked through the Loss Determination condition (c223), which measures loss by the business's Net Income and operating expenses rather than by rents.
"Suspension" turns on the premises being "rendered untenantable", a term the form leaves undefined although it triggers rental-value coverage.

"[A]ppears to be part of an effort to coerce a civilian population" makes the definition turn on appearances without saying to whom, and the $5 million carve-back cross-refers to a paragraph of another definition.
It replaces the Common Policy Condition on cancellation (c008) with substantially the same notice periods plus a duty to state reasons, leaving two versions of the same condition in the policy.
It requires 60 days' notice of nonrenewal, while the CGL condition When We Do Not Renew (c307) requires only 30 days' notice for that Coverage Part.
It sets a 5-year suit limitation replacing the 2-year limitation still printed in the Commercial Property Conditions (c026), so the policy carries two different limitation periods.
Defining actual cash value as repair or replacement cost "less allowance for deterioration and depreciation, including obsolescence" leaves the method and measure of that allowance entirely open.

This added definition supplies the depreciation-based figure that the Valuation condition (c121) uses, but the Coinsurance condition (c126) speaks only of "the value of Covered Property at the time of loss" and does not say whether this definition or replacement cost supplies it.

The provision applies "when coverage is provided for townhouse buildings and structures", but the Declarations describe the insured premises as apartment buildings and a storage building (c002), so its field of operation is unclear.

Limb b. says the insured's "failure to comply with any warranty or condition" will not affect the insurance if beyond its control, and the very next sentence says that if "you violate a condition of this Coverage Part, we will not pay for loss or damage at the involved location".
It supersedes the Control Of Property condition (c023-c024), whose broader rule that acts of others beyond your control "will not affect this insurance" remains printed in the policy.

Adding an exclusion for "[h]ousehold and personal property, unless owned by the Association of Townhouse Owners" to Property Not Covered has no obvious application to the apartment buildings described in the Declarations (c002).
It replaces the Mortgageholders paragraph b. (c129) with payment to an Insurance Trustee and an Association "as shown in the Townhouse Declaration", a document this policy does not contain.
It raises the per-plant sub-limit to $500 while the Outdoor Property Coverage Extension (c088) still prints $250.
It amends the Builders' Risk Coverage Form and overrides the Transfer Of Rights Of Recovery condition (c033), but no Builders' Risk form is scheduled in this policy's Declarations.

The clause first says "either may make a written request for an appraisal" and then that "an appraisal will be made only if both you and we agree, voluntarily", so the right it grants is withdrawn in the next sentence.

It replaces the Appraisal Loss Condition (c101), which makes appraisal available on one party's written demand, and does not say whether it also displaces the separate Appraisal condition in the Business Income form (c213).

It replaces the Concealment, Misrepresentation Or Fraud condition (c022), dropping that condition's requirement that a concealment be intentional and substituting non-payment for avoidance of the whole Coverage Part.
"[Y]ou" is extended here to any other person or organization qualifying as a Named Insured, while the property forms (c047, c186) confine "you" to the Named Insured shown in the Declarations.

"[T]hose sums that the insured becomes legally obligated to pay as damages" and the duty to defend "any 'suit' seeking those damages" leave the boundary between defence and indemnity to be worked out from the allegations.
The known-loss condition turns on whether an insured "knew that the 'bodily injury' or 'property damage' had occurred, in whole or in part", a partial-knowledge test the clause does not calibrate.

Two printed columns have run together, so the Contractual Liability, Liquor, Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability exclusions are interleaved sentence by sentence and none can be read continuously.
Exclusion m. is corrupted ("'Personai would nob place, in whole or in ... afigi' or bacterla"), leaving the pollution and related exclusions unreadable as printed.

Which limb applies depends on how the insured "is designated in the Declarations", and the Commercial General Liability Declarations (c005) state "THE INSURED IS: CORPORATION" while the named insured is Boardwalk Apartments LC, a limited liability company.
"[A]cting as your real estate manager" is not defined, and the Declarations show the insured operating through Terrace Management Service.
It is expressed as "[s]ubject to 2. above", but the Each Occurrence Limit paragraph the neighbouring provisions call "5." is not reproduced anywhere in this Section III text.

The sentence is scrambled ("the Damage To Premises Pe arising out of any one 'occurrence'. Covers To You Limit is the most we will pay"), with a fragment of the Each Occurrence Limit dropped into the middle of it.
It is made "[s]ubject to 5. above", but paragraph 5 of Section III does not appear in the policy text as reproduced.
Notice is owed "as soon as practicable" of an occurrence "which may result in a claim", a double standard of timing and likelihood that the condition does not fix.
The paragraph breaks off mid-sentence ("Then, we will share ... scribed inc. below"), so the sharing rule it invokes is not stated.

Audited earned premium may exceed the advance premium stated in the Declarations, which sits uneasily with the Non-Assessable condition (c046) promising the insured is not liable for any premium other than that stated in the policy.
It requires only 30 days' notice of nonrenewal, while the Kansas Changes Nonrenewal provision (c249) requires 60 days' notice stating reasons for this policy.
"'Bodily injury' means bodily injury, sickness or disease" defines the term by repeating it, leaving whether purely emotional injury is included unresolved.
"[O]ne which becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be" gives no test for when a fire that was never "intended" at all is hostile.

Limb f. is a general catch-all — "that part of any other contract or agreement pertaining to your business ... under which you assume the tort liability of another" — sitting after five narrowly enumerated agreement types, leaving its reach open to an ejusdem generis argument.
"'Occurrence' means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions" defines the term by an undefined word, "accident".

Limb c. covers "wrongful eviction from, wrongful entry into, or invasion of the right of private occupancy of a room, dwelling or premises" committed by or on behalf of "its owner, landlord or lessor", and the boundary of "invasion of the right of private occupancy" is not fixed.

The closing paragraph is corrupted ("or the purposes of this insurance, electronic dala © ivy not tangible property. s used in this definttion ..."), so the electronic-data carve-out cannot be read as written.
The "Your product" definition runs into the separate "Your work" definition mid-paragraph, so limbs b. and c. of each are interleaved and neither definition is complete.

The enumeration is corrupted ("a Any supervision" for item 5 and "&. Any obligation" for item 6), so the cross-references to "parts 1. through 4." and "parts 1. through 5." do not line up with the list.
The Coverage A and Coverage B versions of the exclusion have run together into a single interleaved block, so the exclusion added to Coverage A cannot be read apart from the Coverage B text.

This entry reproduces the same interleaved Coverage A/Coverage B text as the preceding provision and then repeats the "This exclusion applies" paragraph, so the same words appear twice as separate provisions.
